prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, hip-cut demi statue portrait, a 10-cell wood-only grid body (5 rows, two columns), every cell physically stepped, no bare skin below the collarbones. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually finished thigh-stub tips just below her hip line, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her form comes to an end, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Korean woman in girl-crush makeup — fair ivory skin, sharply angled thin brows, a razor-sharp winged cat-eye liner extending far past the outer corner, deep brown-black eyeshadow, long lashes, large eyes with bright real catchlights, strongly sculpted contour, a deep wine-red matte lip, long sleek black hair, a cold, commanding gaze. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. On each ear a big black-steel hoop and a thick bar.

Physique: Her waist cinched to an impossible minimum, making the contrast with the enormous rear utterly extreme: the rear and hips flare to more than four times the width of that narrow waist, an enormous rounded rear projecting far out behind her and merging into the lower back and thighs as one continuous mass, a moderate chest, slim shoulders, body divided into a 10-cell grid (5 rows, two columns), each cell a different wood variant, stepped seams.

Boundary: a single straight, flat line runs around the base of the neck and across both collarbones, never jagged, never zigzag — real skin above, material immediately below, no skin anywhere lower. At that line, the material's edge rises in a small raised step, casting a crisp shadow.

Below the collarbones, her body is divided into a grid of 10 cells — 5 horizontal rows stacked top to bottom, crossed by one vertical line down the centre splitting each row into a left and right cell — each cell with a raised stepped edge and shadow at every border, no gaps, no skin anywhere, every cell a genuinely different variant of the same wood material family. Row 1 (her whole left arm and left chest / her whole right arm and right chest): left cell carved solid dark wenge wood with fine gold-tan pinstripes, completely opaque; right cell carved solid vivid violet-purple purpleheart wood, completely opaque. Row 2 (left / right body band 2): left cell carved solid golden teak with fine straight grain, completely opaque; right cell carved solid warm cream-to-tan olive wood with dark swirling grain, completely opaque. Row 3 (left / right body band 3): left cell carved solid vivid orange-red Osage orange wood, completely opaque; right cell carved solid dark chocolate-brown bocote wood with bold tiger-stripe patterns, completely opaque. Row 4 (left / right body band 4): left cell carved solid striking orange-red padauk wood, completely opaque; right cell carved solid richly streaked cream, rose-pink and violet Brazilian tulipwood, completely opaque. Row 5 (left thigh-stub tip / right thigh-stub tip): left cell carved solid deep black ebony with fine dense grain, completely opaque, rounding off at its tip; right cell carved solid deep reddish-brown rosewood streaked with black, completely opaque, rounding off at its tip.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a deep royal blue on one side and a warm golden orange on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, her left hand resting on her flared hip, her right arm held clear of her body, the hand relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so blue light glances off one side and orange light glances off the other, catching a crisp glint along every stepped seam in the grid. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
